reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is ensuring that our model's predicted probabilities align with empirical frequencies. We formalize this via calibration, which equates the conditional probability of an event given its predicted likelihood to that predicted likelihood itself. The empirical test involves sorting predictions into deciles, computing the mean predicted probability and observed event frequency within each bin. Perfect calibration manifests as points along the 45-degree line. In adversarial sports markets, miscalibrated models create exploitable inefficiencies; calibration thus serves as a fundamental veto condition against overconfident or misspecified forecasts.
